es: Reparar con el mínimo cambio frases con errores de gramática oral, concesión, contingencia, registro y narración, y decidir cuánto hay que tocar para conservar la voz del autor.

vocabulary.es: revisar un texto en busca de erratas

teaching.en: Flag the error first, then repair only the words that are wrong, because a minimal change keeps your own voice intact.
teaching.es: Marca primero el error y repara solo las palabras que fallan, porque un cambio mínimo conserva tu propia voz.
teaching.explanationEs: Corregir lo mínimo te enseña qué regla falló; reescribirlo todo solo esconde el error.
segments: Flag the error first, then repair only the words that are
wrong, because a minimal change keeps your own voice intact.
teaching.audioText: Flag the error first, then repair only the words that are wrong, because a minimal change keeps your own voice intact.

teaching.en: A consistent story needs no unexplained shift in tense: When I arrived, the meeting had already started, and everyone was waiting.
teaching.es: Un relato coherente no admite un cambio de tiempo verbal sin motivo: Cuando llegué, la reunión ya había empezado y todos esperaban.
teaching.explanationEs: Si dos hechos pasados se suceden, el anterior lleva had + participio.
segments: A consistent story needs no unexplained shift in tense: When I
arrived, the meeting had already started, and everyone was waiting.
teaching.audioText: A consistent story needs no unexplained shift in tense: When I arrived, the meeting had already started, and everyone was waiting.

teaching.en: However precise the wording may be, the message can still sound rude, because precision is not the same as tact.
teaching.es: Por preciso que sea el texto, el mensaje puede seguir sonando grosero, porque precisión no es lo mismo que tacto.
teaching.explanationEs: However + adjetivo: el adjetivo va pegado a however y luego viene el sujeto, sin inversión.
segments: However precise the wording may be, the message can still
sound rude, because precision is not the same as tact.
teaching.audioText: However precise the wording may be, the message can still sound rude, because precision is not the same as tact.

teaching.en: Formal wording for a contingency plan uses inverted should: Should the contractor fail to deliver, penalties apply.
teaching.es: La redacción formal de un plan de contingencia usa should invertido: Si el contratista no cumple, se aplican sanciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Should + sujeto + verbo base sustituye a if; el verbo no lleva -s.
segments: Formal wording for a contingency plan uses inverted should:
Should the contractor fail to deliver, penalties apply.
teaching.audioText: Formal wording for a contingency plan uses inverted should: Should the contractor fail to deliver, penalties apply.

teaching.en: When you proofread, swap out a verb for a noun where you can: prices fell becomes the fall in prices.
teaching.es: Cuando revises el texto, sustituye un verbo por un sustantivo donde puedas: prices fell pasa a the fall in prices.
teaching.explanationEs: Nominalizar compacta la idea; el sustantivo de cambio lleva in para lo que cambia.
segments: When you proofread, swap out a verb for a noun
where you can: prices fell becomes the fall in prices.
teaching.audioText: When you proofread, swap out a verb for a noun where you can: prices fell becomes the fall in prices.

teaching.en: Iron out a blunt request with an indirect question: I was wondering whether the wording could be softer.
teaching.es: Pule una petición demasiado directa con una pregunta indirecta: Me preguntaba si la redacción podría ser más suave.
teaching.explanationEs: En la pregunta indirecta el orden es afirmativo (the wording could), sin inversión.
segments: Iron out a blunt request with an indirect question:
I was wondering whether the wording could be softer.
teaching.audioText: Iron out a blunt request with an indirect question: I was wondering whether the wording could be softer.

prompt.es: Repara la respuesta de Tom, que quiere decir «yo tampoco».

choices.text: Neither I haven't.
Nor I have.
Neither have I.

feedback.es: Tras neither, el auxiliar se adelanta al sujeto: Neither have I. No se repite el verbo entero ni se añade otra negación.

hint.es: Tras neither, el auxiliar pasa delante del sujeto.

origin.text: At the climbing club, Leo admitted that he had never tried a proper wall. Tom nodded warmly and answered: Neither I have. The instructor smiled and handed them both a helmet.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aunque estaba cansado, terminé el informe antes de medianoche.»

feedback.es: Adjetivo + though/as + sujeto + verbo expresa la concesión sin inversión ni but.

hint.es: Hace falta una conjunción concesiva colocada tras el adjetivo.

origin.text: The deadline was close, and the office was noisy. Tired ___ I was, I finished the report before midnight.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En caso de lluvia, el partido se trasladará.»

answer.text: In the event of rain, the match will be moved
accepted: In the event of rain, the match will be moved
The match will be moved in the event of rain

feedback.es: In the event of + nombre abre la contingencia formal y después va la consecuencia.

hint.es: Empieza por la condición y deja la consecuencia para el final.

prompt.es: El informe marca la segunda cláusula como imprecisa: elige la reparación mínima.

choices.text: Prices fell sharply in March, and the demand for tickets fell with them.
Prices fell sharply in March, and the demand to tickets fell with them.
Prices fell sharply in March, and the demand about tickets fell with them.

feedback.es: La preposición que acompaña a demand es for: the demand for tickets. Se cambia una sola palabra y el resto de la frase se respeta.

origin.text: Draft report, line four: Prices fell sharply in March, and the demand of tickets fell with them. The writer has flagged the second clause because it is not precise.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el tutor para reparar la frase de Sara.

choices.text: He changes reached to a present form to match the story.
He adds a single auxiliary to show which event came first.
He rewrites the sentence so that the train arrives later.

feedback.es: El tutor solo añade had: la salida del tren ocurrió antes de la llegada y el pasado perfecto lo muestra con un cambio mínimo.

origin.audio: Sara wrote: The train already left when we reached the platform. Her tutor underlined left and explained that the departure happened before the arrival, so the verb needs a past perfect. He did not rewrite the sentence. He added one small word, and the order of events became clear.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con error con su reparación mínima.

pairs: Should the weather gets worse, we will cancel

pairs.es: Forma base tras should: Should the weather get worse

pairs: However is the room small, it is comfortable

pairs.es: Sin inversión: However small the room is

pairs: I wondered where was the manager

pairs.es: Orden afirmativo: where the manager was

pairs: The increase of prices surprised us
When Mia called, the shop already closed

pairs.es: Anterioridad: lo previo pide had already closed

feedback.es: Cada reparación toca una sola palabra o una sola posición: la forma base, la inversión sobrante, el orden de la pregunta, la preposición y el tiempo de lo anterior.

prompt.es: ¿Qué critica la tutora de la corrección que hizo Tom?

choices.text: That he left the main error in the second clause as it was.
That he replaced formal wording with a much more casual style.
That he missed the shift in tense that she had flagged.
That he changed more of the text than the errors required.

feedback.es: La tutora dice que cambió seis palabras cuando solo dos fallaban y que una buena reparación conserva la voz del autor: critica el exceso de cambios.

origin.text: Your repaired version changes six words, yet only two of them were wrong. The original clause, Should sales falls, was nearly right: once the extra s is removed, nothing else needs to change. You did not have to rewrite it as If sales were to fall. A good repair fixes the rule and keeps the voice of the writer, so next time flag the error, swap out one word and stop.

prompt.es: Escucha a la editora y elige qué postura adopta ante la norma del manual.

choices.text: She accepts the rule for formal documents but resists applying it everywhere.
She regrets the rule and would like to see it removed from the guide.
She supports the rule in every document because it is short and formal.
She wants contracts to use a plain if and emails to use should.

feedback.es: La editora ve la lógica de la norma para contratos e informes, pero defiende un if sencillo en correos: acepta la norma con reservas.

origin.audio: When we drafted our style guide last spring, several of us argued for a single pattern, and I was one of them. The guide now says that every contingency clause must begin with should, and I still see the logic: the pattern is short and formal. In an email to a colleague, though, Should it rain, the match will be postponed can sound stiff. I would keep the rule for contracts and reports, and leave emails free to use a plain if. Asking every reader to accept one pattern would only make our writing less natural. Having tested it on real emails, I have changed my mind.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si el proveedor no entrega a tiempo, se aplicará el plan.»

feedback.es: Should + sujeto + verbo base sustituye a if en una contingencia formal: Should the supplier fail.

origin.text: The contract includes a contingency plan. ___ the supplier fail to deliver on time, the plan will apply.

prompt.es: Repara las tres frases con el mínimo cambio: tiempo, contingencia y tacto.

answer.text: When we reached the cinema, the film had already started. Should the roof leak, we will call the owner. I was wondering where we could meet.
accepted: When we reached the cinema, the film had already started. Should the roof leak, we will call the owner. I was wondering where we could meet.
When we reached the cinema, the film had already started. Should the roof leak, we would call the owner. I was wondering whether we could meet.

feedback.es: Los tres errores se arreglan con una palabra o un orden: had already started, Should the roof leak y where we could meet.

origin.text: When we reached the cinema, the film already started. Should the roof leaks, we will call the owner. I was wondering where could we meet.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por fuerte que suene la música, ella sigue estudiando.»

answer.text: However loud the music is, she keeps studying
accepted: However loud the music is, she keeps studying
However loud the music may be, she keeps studying

feedback.es: However + adjetivo va antes del sujeto: However loud the music is, sin inversión.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el autor sobre la reparación más formal posible?

choices.text: That formal repairs should be avoided in every kind of message.
That the most formal version is not always the best choice for the reader.
That teammates dislike correct sentences that contain should.
That a repair should keep the wording as close to the original as possible.

feedback.es: El autor admite que la frase es correcta y precisa, pero fría para unos compañeros: lo formal no siempre es lo mejor para el lector.

origin.text: A repaired sentence that reads as if a committee had written it is not a good repair. Consider Should it rain, the match will be postponed. It is formal, precise and correct, yet in a message to teammates it would sound cold. The skill lies in matching the wording to the reader, not in applying the strictest rule available.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia pidió a Leo ayuda para afinar la redacción y pulir los últimos fallos.»

feedback.es: Tighten up significa hacer un texto más ajustado; junto a iron out describe el pulido final de un borrador.

origin.text: The first draft rambled, so Mia asked Leo to help her ___ up the wording and iron out the last few errors before the deadline.
